title.en: UAE Type Approval Policy Version 4 is now effective

summary.en: TDRA’s unified Type Approval Policy Version 4 became effective on 1 May 2026 and consolidates the main policy, requirements, procedures, testing, customs, market surveillance framework.

body.en:
TDRA states that Version 4 is the updated unified regulatory reference for telecommunications equipment and technologies in the UAE.

The policy consolidates previous Type Approval instruments and applies to relevant activities including registration, approval, import, distribution, display, sale and commercial use. The official policy was issued on 21 January 2026 and became effective on 1 May 2026.

For a specific product, the applicable route, technical evidence, service treatment should be checked against the current TDRA system and policy before filing.

whatKnow.en: Use Version 4 as the primary TDRA reference rather than relying on older Version 3 documents.

sourceName: TDRA — Type Approval Policy Version 4 / Official FAQ

title.en: Jordan TRC updates its Type Approval reference and ETAS information

summary.en: TRC’s current Type Approval page provides the regulatory instructions, technical rules, annexes and automated ETAS application route, with the page updated on 3 March 2026.

body.en:
Jordan’s Telecommunications Regulatory Commission provides a dedicated Type Approval reference covering the instructions for telecommunications devices, technical rules and standards, annexes and the automated ETAS system.

The TRC service guide describes an online process: create an ETAS account, submit the application, upload the service requirements, complete the application process and receive the official approval letter when the requirements are complete.

Manufacturers should use the current TRC instructions and technical rules when preparing a Jordan submission.

whatKnow.en: Jordan applications are coordinated through the ETAS route, so the technical file should be prepared for online submission and the current TRC requirements.

sourceName: Jordan TRC — Type Approvals for Telecom Equipment

title.en: Algeria updates electronic communications equipment approval framework

summary.en: ARPCE announced publication of Executive Decree No. 26-97 dated 31 January 2026, establishing conditions and procedures for approval of electronic communications equipment.

body.en:
ARPCE states that Executive Decree No. 26-97 establishes the conditions and procedures for approval of electronic communications equipment.

The framework covers application conditions, processing deadlines, and the issue and validity of the certificate of conformity. ARPCE’s current FAQ states that the response time may not exceed two months from submission of a complete file.

The authority also identifies terminal equipment and radio installations intended for connection to a public electronic communications network among the equipment subject to approval.

whatKnow.en: The 2026 decree should be treated as the current primary approval framework for applicable Algerian equipment.

sourceName: ARPCE — Executive Decree No. 26-97 / Approval FAQ

title.en: Egypt NTRA publishes updated 2026 Type Approval schemes

summary.en: NTRA currently applies Light, Intermediate and Tight Type Approval schemes and provides 2026 procedure documents and a scheme-determination process.

body.en:
NTRA’s current Type Approval procedure page identifies three schemes: Light, Intermediate and Tight.

The authority provides 2026 procedure documents and a scheme determination chart/interactive questions to identify the route applicable to a product. The procedure also includes the associated forms.

Manufacturers should determine the applicable scheme before preparing the final evidence package, because testing and documentation can differ by route.

whatKnow.en: Do not assume one approval route applies to every product. The NTRA scheme must be determined from the product characteristics and applicable country category.

title.en: Saudi Arabia Updates Wireless Regulatory Requirements for ICT Equipment

summary.en: Saudi Arabia has introduced important regulatory changes affecting wireless ICT equipment, with updated conformity and market-access requirements for manufacturers and importers of connected and radio-enabled devices

body.en:
Saudi Arabia has introduced important regulatory changes affecting wireless Information and Communication Technology (ICT) equipment, reinforcing the requirements that manufacturers and importers need to consider when placing connected and radio-enabled products on the Saudi market.

The regulatory framework involves both the Communications, Space & Technology Commission (CST) and the Saudi Standards, Metrology and Quality Organization (SASO), with requirements applying according to the type and characteristics of the equipment.

### What Products May Be Affected?

The requirements are particularly relevant to products that incorporate wireless or radio functionality, including:

* Wireless networking equipment and routers
* Cellular and mobile devices
* Internet of Things (IoT) equipment
* Short-range wireless devices
* Radio-frequency (RF) equipment
* Connected ICT products
* Other devices operating through regulated radio technologies

Manufacturers should identify the applicable technical and conformity requirements before shipping products to Saudi Arabia.

### Regulatory Compliance and Market Access

For international manufacturers, understanding the relationship between technical regulations, conformity assessment, product certification and telecommunications requirements is an important part of the Saudi market-entry process.

Depending on the product category, manufacturers may need to complete applicable conformity procedures and ensure that the equipment meets the relevant Saudi technical requirements before importation and commercialization.

The CST continues to play a central role in regulating telecommunications and ICT equipment, including requirements related to telecommunications devices, radio equipment and spectrum use.

### What Manufacturers Should Consider

Companies planning to introduce wireless products into Saudi Arabia should review their products before shipment and determine:

* The applicable Saudi technical requirements
* Whether the product falls within telecommunications or radio equipment regulations
* Applicable conformity assessment requirements
* Required technical documentation and test reports
* Radio-frequency and spectrum-related requirements, where applicable
* Import and market-access requirements

Early regulatory assessment can help manufacturers avoid unnecessary delays during the approval and import process.

### AFAQ JOOD Regulatory Support

AFAQ JOOD supports international manufacturers, exporters and technology companies with Type Approval and regulatory compliance coordination across selected markets in the Middle East and Africa.

Our team helps clients understand applicable requirements, organize technical documentation and coordinate regulatory procedures with the relevant authorities and local stakeholders.

For companies planning to enter the Saudi Arabian market, obtaining a clear understanding of the applicable regulatory pathway at an early stage can help make the market-access process more structured and efficient.

**Regulatory requirements may vary depending on the product type, technology, frequency bands and applicable Saudi regulations. Manufacturers should verify the requirements applicable to their specific product before market entry.**

whatKnow.en:
Manufacturers planning to introduce wireless and ICT equipment into the Saudi Arabian market should assess the applicable regulatory requirements before shipment.

The requirements may vary depending on the product category, wireless technologies, frequency bands, intended use and applicable Saudi technical regulations. Manufacturers should therefore:

* Identify the applicable regulatory and technical requirements for the product.
* Confirm whether the equipment falls under telecommunications, radio or other regulated product categories.
* Prepare the required technical documentation and relevant test reports.
* Verify conformity assessment and certification requirements before importation.
* Review applicable radio-frequency and spectrum requirements for wireless products.
* Ensure that product information and documentation are consistent across the regulatory submission.
* Confirm the applicable market-access procedures before commercializing the product in Saudi Arabia.

Early regulatory assessment can help manufacturers identify potential compliance issues and reduce delays during the market-entry process.
